title: Arancini
subtitle: Crisp fried risotto balls with mozzarella centres
excerpt: Cold leftover risotto shaped around a cube of mozzarella, coated in flour, egg and panko breadcrumbs, then deep-fried until golden. If you don't have leftover risotto, the recipe includes instructions for cooking the rice base from scratch. The mozzarella centre melts during frying into a stringy pocket that pulls apart when you break them open.
sourceNotes: Arancini originate in Sicily, where they have been made since at least the 10th century during Arab rule; the name means 'little oranges' in Sicilian dialect, referring to their golden colour and round shape.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Shape the arancini and refrigerate, uncovered, for up to 4 hours before frying. This helps the coating adhere.

content.text: The risotto base must be cold before you shape the arancini; warm rice will not hold together. If making the rice from scratch, spread it on a tray and refrigerate for at least 2 hours. The coating goes on in the standard order: flour, then beaten egg, then panko. The panko gives a much crispier crust than regular breadcrumbs and stays crunchier for longer after frying.

Make the risotto base: melt the butter in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until softened. Add the arborio rice and stir for 1 minute until the grains are coated. Add the warm stock a ladleful at a time, stirring after each addition until absorbed, for about 20 minutes. Remove from the heat, stir in the parmesan and season. Spread on a tray and refrigerate until completely cold, at least 2 hours.

Set up three shallow bowls: one with flour, one with the beaten eggs, one with the panko. Take about 60g of cold risotto, flatten it in your palm, place a cube of mozzarella in the centre and close the rice around it, shaping into a firm ball. Repeat with the remaining rice and mozzarella.
Roll each ball in flour, shake off the excess, dip in beaten egg, then coat generously in panko. Press the panko in firmly so it sticks. Place on a tray. Refrigerate for 20 minutes if time allows.

Pour the sunflower oil into a large, deep saucepan to a depth of at least 6cm. Heat to 180C. Fry the arancini in batches of 3 to 4 for 3 to 4 minutes, turning gently, until deep golden all over. Drain on kitchen paper, season immediately with salt and serve hot.

items.symptom: Arancini are splitting open in the oil
items.cause: The rice was not cold enough when shaped, or they were not refrigerated before frying
items.fix: Remove from the oil and return to the fridge for 30 minutes. Next time ensure the risotto is fully cold before shaping, and refrigerate the shaped balls before frying.

items.cause: The mozzarella cubes were too large or the frying time was too short
items.fix: Cut the mozzarella into smaller 1cm cubes and ensure a full 4 minutes of frying at 180C. The outside should be deeply golden before they come out.
